sourceOccurrences.label: Translated-box exit inequality
sourceOccurrences.note: 0VB3 counts centre intervals and retains the bond probability, before applying the power-law upper bound. The decomposition itself works for every positive alpha.

sourceOccurrences.label: Analytic contraction over scales
sourceOccurrences.note: PIZX separates the averaged bound and exit inequality from percolation. The short-distance factor epsilon^(1-alpha) contracts; the far shells sum as2^(-dl).

sourceOccurrences.label: Critical upper bound and localization input
sourceOccurrences.locator: Proposition2.1; upper half of Theorem1.4; PartII cited input to random-box localization
sourceOccurrences.note: TGF9 combines MRZO,0VB3 andPIZX. Monotone domination supplies the upper input toYUHF for finite-range cutoffs; a cutoff susceptibility lower bound remains separate.

sourceOccurrences.label: Internal finite-size criterion
sourceOccurrences.note: AXYA proves the stronger internal-mean formulation by averaging the boundary functional and applying the finite-size criterion.

sourceOccurrences.label: Half-susceptibility radius and confined clusters
sourceOccurrences.locator: Corollary 2.5 and Proposition 2.3, printed p.10/PDF index9; HTML235–255
sourceOccurrences.note: 6G4B retains both power envelopes and proves uniform susceptibility comparison and saturation of internal box means. The upper-only corollary has an explicit nearest-neighbour counterexample.

sourceOccurrences.label: Separated weighted kernel convolution
sourceOccurrences.note: SFR0 bounds each weighted row before applying separation of the middle kernel; 0<alpha<1 and the regularized origin are explicit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Near-critical upper bound
sourceOccurrences.locator: Proposition 2.3 / proof headed Theorem 1.5, equations (2.5)–(2.6), printed pp.11–12/PDF indices10–11; HTML277–310
sourceOccurrences.note: CQK2 uses two independent box centres, the original short-edge restriction and a finite truncated amplitude. YUHF supplies finiteness using TGF9, without a cutoff susceptibility lower bound.

sourceOccurrences.label: Confined pointwise lower bound
sourceOccurrences.note: Two independent induced root clusters have internal mean of order n^alpha by 6G4B. The critical full-window quantile and rooted damping preserve that first moment in the second-moment bound. All pairs of joining bonds are counted, including shared endpoints.

sourceOccurrences.label: Triangle growth at the crossover scale
sourceOccurrences.locator: Section 2.3, proof of Theorem 1.1 through equation (2.7), printed p.13/PDF index12; HTML314–334
sourceOccurrences.note: Dyadic largest-side shells prove bounded/logarithmic/power growth without requiring the intermediate inner convolution estimate 2alpha<d. The distance-to-criticality conversion and mean-field consequences remain separate.

sourceOccurrences.label: Theorem 1.1: all three mean-field consequences
sourceOccurrences.locator: Theorem 1.1, printed pp.3–4; section 2.3 conclusion, printed p.13/PDF index12
sourceOccurrences.note: Row normalization, the corrected square, self-dependent diagram integration and entropy comparison prove both regimes, with explicit pointwise tail lower bounds.

sourceOccurrences.label: Remark 2.7: susceptibility bound with corrected differential premise
sourceOccurrences.locator: Remark 2.7, printed p.14/PDF index13, extracted lines1066–1085
sourceOccurrences.note: The diagram exponent q=3-d/alpha lies below one half, so integration gives the stated susceptibility power at the finite critical endpoint.

sourceOccurrences.note: Entropy comparison applies when g<2; the integrated lower tail and logarithmic limits bound any existing exponents and squeeze their limiting values.

Separated endpoints use two spatial averages; nearby endpoints use the previous scale and an integrable short-distance shell sum; far endpoints retain the kernel exponent before the geometric sum.
